status: Native cumulative draft; separate exports and remote runner pending

steps.title: Trace the bits before writing code

quiz.prompt: Which quantity is an alphabet index?

steps.expectedObservation: The sextets19,22,5,46 select TWFu.

hints.text: Account for the same twenty-four bits on both sides of the conversion.
Write three eight-bit rows, then mark boundaries every six bits across the joined rows.

steps.prose: Use the Man example to account for all twenty-four input bits. Identify which two sextets share each byte boundary before running the starter. Keep numerical sextets separate from ASCII codes.

steps.title: Bound the input before sizing output

quiz.prompt: When is adding two to the count safe?

choices.text: After the unsigned bound has been established.

steps.expectedObservation: A three-byte request needs four output bytes; insufficient capacity returns before reading source.

hints.text: Establish the unsigned bound before performing length arithmetic.
After rejecting counts above 4096, compute four times the integer quotient of count plus two divided by three; compare with capacity.

steps.title: Retain counts and pointers in the encoder frame

quiz.prompt: Which value must remain fixed while the loop walks?

choices.text: The total output count returned on success.

steps.expectedObservation: The fixed output length is four while remaining input is three.

hints.text: Separate the remaining input count from the total promised output count.
Keep advancing input and output pointers in saved registers while retaining the exact output length for the eventual return.

steps.title: Read only the available source bytes

quiz.prompt: Why clear the missing-byte registers?

choices.text: Their zero bits form canonical short-tail sextets.
A byte load always clears every temporary.
The caller guarantees three readable bytes for every tail.

steps.expectedObservation: The Man fixture loads decimal77,97,110 before any output store.

hints.text: A short final group must not load bytes outside the supplied range.
Load the first byte unconditionally for a nonempty group; zero the other temporaries and load each only when the remaining count permits it.

steps.title: Publish the first two sextets

quiz.prompt: What does a sextet select?

steps.expectedObservation: The output prefix is TW, with the other destination bytes still sentinels.

hints.text: A sextet is a number before it becomes a character.
Split the first byte at bit two; combine its low two bits with the high four bits of the second byte before the alphabet lookup.

steps.title: Publish the third character when it exists

quiz.prompt: Which source bits form this third sextet?

choices.text: The second byte low four bits and third byte high two bits.

steps.expectedObservation: For Man, the third sextet is five and the prefix becomes TWF.

hints.text: The third sextet crosses the second byte boundary.
Join the low four bits of the second byte with the high two bits of the third, then look up that six-bit index.

steps.title: Complete a triple and advance by different strides

quiz.prompt: Why are the two pointer strides different?

choices.text: The representation expands three bytes into four characters.
Both pointers must remain word aligned.
The alphabet address advances with the input.

steps.expectedObservation: Man produces TWFu and returns four output bytes.

hints.text: The pointers advance by different amounts on the two sides.
A full group consumes three bytes and reserves four output positions. Finish when the input remainder reaches zero.

steps.title: Write the final one or two pad characters

quiz.prompt: Does a pad represent a decoded zero byte?

choices.text: No; it marks an incomplete input group.

steps.expectedObservation: The one-byte and two-byte recipes produce Zg== and Zm8=.

hints.text: Padding replaces positions whose source bits do not exist.
One source byte requires two equals signs; two source bytes require one. Retain the meaningful earlier alphabet characters.

steps.title: Check short tails independently

quiz.prompt: What determines the number of final pads?

steps.expectedObservation: The three tail shapes have two, one and zero padding characters.

hints.text: Compare the same algorithm at each possible remainder.
Prepare one-, two- and three-byte inputs and inspect all four output positions, including padding and the byte beyond the result.

steps.prose: Use the separate one-byte and two-byte recipes, then the complete triple. Compare the exact four-character outputs and their padding positions. A zero input byte is ordinary binary data, while a pad occupies text without adding binary output.

steps.title: Recognize the uppercase interval

quiz.prompt: Why can zero not indicate an invalid character?

choices.text: A is a valid character with sextet zero.
All invalid characters have value zero.

steps.expectedObservation: ASCII Z reaches the supplied return with sextet25.

hints.text: Test a character interval before subtracting its base.
Uppercase ASCII letters map to zero through twenty-five. Characters below A or above Z must continue to the next range.

steps.title: Map lowercase and numeric intervals

quiz.prompt: What is the numeric range first sextet?

steps.expectedObservation: The digit9 produces sextet61; the lowercase recipe reaches sextet51.

hints.text: Adjacent ASCII intervals do not imply adjacent alphabet indices.
Lowercase letters start at twenty-six; decimal digits start at fifty-two. Subtract the appropriate ASCII base before adding its alphabet base.

steps.title: Handle the final symbols and invalid octets

quiz.prompt: Which value marks unfinished classifier work?

steps.expectedObservation: Plus and slash return62 and63; at-sign returns minus one.

hints.text: The final two valid characters are individual cases.
Map plus to sixty-two and slash to sixty-three; return minus one for every other character after the letter and digit tests.

steps.title: Initialize a provisional decoded size

quiz.prompt: When can padding reduce the provisional size?

choices.text: After its final position and unused bits are validated.
Before the input count is known.

steps.expectedObservation: The four-character fixture starts with provisional size three.

hints.text: Initialize validation state before scanning any characters.
Retain the full text count, a provisional three-per-quartet decoded length and a previous-sextet value for final pad-bit checks.

steps.title: Classify the ordinary characters without output

quiz.prompt: Why retain the previous sextet?

choices.text: Its unused bits must be checked if a pad follows.

steps.expectedObservation: TWFu reaches validation success with provisional size three and no destination writes.

hints.text: A padding character changes which positions may follow it.
For ordinary characters, call the classifier, reject minus one and propagate minus two. Advance only after the character has been accepted.

steps.title: Validate one final pad

quiz.prompt: Which bits are unused before one final pad?

choices.text: All bits of the first byte.
The preceding sextet low two bits.
The first sextet high two bits.

steps.expectedObservation: Zm8= validates to two bytes; the noncanonical recipe fails without output.

hints.text: One equals sign removes one output byte from the provisional length.
Require padding to be in the last position and require the preceding sextet’s low two bits to be zero.

steps.title: Validate the final pair of pads

quiz.prompt: What does the second pad check establish?

choices.text: That both final positions have the required pad form.

steps.expectedObservation: Zg== validates to one byte; Zh== is rejected.

hints.text: Two equals signs leave only one decoded byte in the last quartet.
Require both final pad characters and test the second sextet’s low four bits before subtracting two from the provisional length.

steps.title: Inspect the supplied restores

quiz.prompt: Why cannot four mark an unfinished classifier?

steps.expectedObservation: Every allocated frame is restored before an unfinished result reaches its caller.

hints.text: A nested call changes the return address register.
Trace where each frame saves ra and where every normal, error and development exit restores the full saved state.

steps.prose: Locate each provided frame and its matching development return. Whole routines use development status four, while the classifier uses minus two. That distinction lets a valid sextet four remain numerical data and lets unfinished helpers propagate through nested calls.

steps.title: Reject impossible text counts before reading

quiz.prompt: What happens before the decoder reads text?

choices.text: The output count is guessed from a terminator.
Its count is bounded and checked for quartet alignment.
The first output byte is stored.

steps.expectedObservation: A four-character input reaches the frame; malformed counts return before source access.

hints.text: Some malformed requests can be rejected without reading their pointers.
Handle over-limit and empty counts first, then reject a nonzero text count whose low two bits are not zero.

steps.title: Validate before checking capacity and publishing

quiz.prompt: Which result may be used after successful validation?

choices.text: A count from an unsuccessful helper.
The original capacity as the decoded length.

steps.expectedObservation: TWFu establishes three output bytes while destination remains unchanged.

hints.text: Error precedence determines the order of preflight checks.
Validate the whole text first. Only after successful validation compare its decoded length with destination capacity.

steps.title: Exclude the padded final quartet from vector work

quiz.prompt: Why exclude a padded final quartet?

choices.text: The16-character kernel requires alphabet characters without pads.

steps.expectedObservation: The unpadded TWFu fixture has four vector-eligible characters.

hints.text: A padded final quartet needs scalar handling.
Inspect the final text positions and exclude that quartet from the full-vector body count when padding is present.

steps.title: Read all four characters before storing a byte

quiz.prompt: What protects an in-place quartet from self-corruption?

choices.text: Assume source and output strides are equal.
Load all of its characters before writing decoded bytes.
Store the first byte before reading the second character.

steps.expectedObservation: The private sextets for TWFu are19,22,5,46, and output is untouched.

hints.text: Exact in-place decoding requires reading ahead of output stores.
Classify all four text characters into the private quartet area before publishing any decoded byte.

steps.title: Publish the first decoded byte

quiz.prompt: What determines whether another output store is permitted?

choices.text: Whether the previous byte was zero.
The size of a vector register.

steps.expectedObservation: The partial Man fixture publishes only M before the next unfinished region.

hints.text: The first byte joins the first two sextets.
Shift the first sextet left by two, combine it with the second shifted right by four, then store only if output remains.

steps.title: Publish the second decoded byte

quiz.prompt: Which tail ends after this second store?

choices.text: Every input containing a lowercase letter.

steps.expectedObservation: The partial output becomes Ma, with one output byte still remaining.

hints.text: The middle output byte joins the second and third sextets.
Use the low four bits of the second sextet and the high four bits of the third. Decrement the remaining output count after storing.

steps.title: Complete the quartet and continue

quiz.prompt: Which count belongs in the success return?

choices.text: The source pointer difference divided by two.

steps.expectedObservation: TWFu returns Man; the short final groups return exactly one or two bytes.

hints.text: The final output byte uses the last two sextets.
Join the low two bits of the third sextet with the fourth; advance input by four characters only after this quartet is finished.

steps.title: Follow exact in-place decoding

quiz.prompt: Which overlap is included in this contract?

choices.text: Only overlapping buffers of equal lengths.

steps.expectedObservation: The decoded prefix changes while the remaining source suffix stays intact.

hints.text: Compare consumed input with published output throughout the loop.
At each in-place quartet boundary, mark four input positions already read and at most three output positions already written.

steps.prose: The scalar decoder loads a whole quartet before writing its first output byte. Source then advances four while output advances three. Trace a second quartet to see why unread text stays ahead of the output pointer.

steps.title: Copy exactly twelve bytes to private storage

quiz.prompt: Where may the kernel safely load sixteen bytes here?

steps.expectedObservation: The private object holds twelve input bytes followed by four zeros.

hints.text: A sixteen-byte vector load cannot read directly from a twelve-byte object.
Copy exactly twelve caller bytes into the private sixteen-byte area and explicitly zero the four remaining positions before loading the vector.

steps.title: Gather the left contribution to each sextet

quiz.prompt: What did the gather destination hold before vshf?

steps.expectedObservation: The working vector holds the shifted left contribution for all sixteen sextets.

hints.text: Each sextet has a left contribution and sometimes a right contribution.
Use the lane-selector and shift tables to place the appropriate first source byte contribution into every output lane.

steps.title: Join the right contribution and mask sextets

quiz.prompt: Which representation is present before alphabet translation?

steps.expectedObservation: The sixteen byte lanes equal the canonical text sextet values.

hints.text: The join must leave exactly six useful bits in each lane.
Gather the complementary source bytes, shift them, OR the contributions and mask every lane with sixty-three.

steps.title: Apply the first alphabet correction

quiz.prompt: Why AND the comparison result with six?

choices.text: It selects the sixth source byte.
It converts an all-one mask into the needed correction.

steps.expectedObservation: Only sextets above25 receive the correction six.

hints.text: Start translation with a common base and then correct intervals.
For sextets at least twenty-six, add the correction for the lowercase alphabet interval; inspect the mask separately from the corrected bytes.

steps.title: Apply the numeric-range correction

quiz.prompt: Must every intermediate byte be printable ASCII?

choices.text: No; only the completed translation must be.

steps.expectedObservation: The lane for sextet52 reaches239 before the final base addition.

hints.text: A later interval may need to undo part of an earlier correction.
For sextets at least fifty-two, subtract the additional correction that moves the numeric interval to its ASCII digit positions.

steps.title: Distinguish plus and slash at the upper end

quiz.prompt: Which vector must the threshold tests read?

steps.expectedObservation: The two symbol lanes now differ by the correction needed for plus and slash.

hints.text: The two largest indices do not continue the digit interval.
Correct sextet sixty-two to plus and sextet sixty-three to slash before adding the common ASCII base.

steps.title: Add the common ASCII base and store sixteen bytes

quiz.prompt: How many caller bytes does this kernel publish?

steps.expectedObservation: The complete text is AZaz09+/Az09+/Za for this kernel recipe.

hints.text: Publication changes caller memory; prior vector calculations do not.
Add ASCII A to the corrected lanes, store exactly sixteen output bytes and then continue through the supplied restore.

steps.title: Build the uppercase character contribution

quiz.prompt: Why can a valid uppercase contribution be zero?

steps.expectedObservation: The accumulator contains uppercase contributions while other character lanes remain zero.

hints.text: Only matching lanes should contribute to the result.
Make an uppercase interval mask, subtract ASCII A and AND the values with that mask before starting the accumulated sextet vector.

steps.title: Add the lowercase contribution

quiz.prompt: Why is OR suitable for merging these contributions?

steps.expectedObservation: Lowercase lanes receive values26 through51.

hints.text: A disjoint interval can be merged without altering previous lanes.
Mask lowercase letters, subtract ASCII a, add twenty-six and OR those contributions into the accumulated sextets.

steps.title: Add the digit contribution

quiz.prompt: What sextet does ASCII zero represent?

steps.expectedObservation: Digit lanes now have their numerical sextets without changing letter lanes.

hints.text: Numeric characters have alphabet indices above both letter intervals.
Mask the zero-through-nine ASCII interval, subtract ASCII zero, add fifty-two and merge the result.

steps.title: Complete the validated sextet vector

quiz.prompt: Where was invalid text rejected?

choices.text: In the complete preflight validation pass.
By treating zero sextets as invalid.

steps.expectedObservation: All sixteen lanes match the expected alphabet values.

hints.text: The direct kernel already assumes validated, unpadded text.
Create equality masks for plus and slash, insert sixty-two and sixty-three, and check the complete sextet vector before packing.

steps.title: Form the first packed byte contribution

quiz.prompt: What does the fourth position represent?

choices.text: Private packing space to be removed.
A caller output zero that must be stored.

steps.expectedObservation: Each four-byte group has its shifted left contribution and a zero fourth byte.

hints.text: Packing reverses the earlier bit regrouping.
Select the sextets that supply each packed byte’s left portion, shift within lanes and mask away bits that do not belong to that byte.

steps.title: Join and compact the twelve useful bytes

quiz.prompt: Why is another gather needed after packing?

choices.text: It adds the missing output terminator.
Useful bytes are separated by group padding positions.

steps.expectedObservation: The compact vector has twelve decoded bytes followed by four private zeros.

hints.text: The packed groups still contain an unused position after each triple.
Merge right contributions, then gather positions zero, one, two, four, five, six and the corresponding later triples; select zeros for the last four lanes.

steps.title: Store privately before the exact caller copy

quiz.prompt: Which store would violate this output contract?

choices.text: Twelve byte stores within the output.
A sixteen-byte store to the caller.
A sixteen-byte store to private storage.

steps.expectedObservation: Exactly twelve caller bytes change; the following bytes remain sentinels.

hints.text: The caller owns twelve output bytes, even though the vector has sixteen lanes.
Store the vector into private storage, then copy exactly its first twelve bytes to the caller destination.

steps.title: Integrate full vector groups with the scalar tail

quiz.prompt: How many raw bytes remain after two kernels consume25 input bytes?

steps.expectedObservation: The25-byte recipe uses two vector groups and a one-byte padded scalar tail.

hints.text: The scalar tail and vector body must share a single remaining-count invariant.
Process twelve input bytes per vector call, advance output by sixteen, propagate a nonzero kernel status and hand a smaller remainder to scalar encoding.

steps.title: Integrate unpadded vector groups and exact tails

quiz.prompt: Which count controls vector eligibility?

steps.expectedObservation: The25-byte decoded result includes a final scalar byte and preserves all following input bytes in place.

hints.text: Validation and padding decisions belong outside the direct vector kernel.
Decode only complete unpadded sixteen-character groups, advance output by twelve and retain the final padded or short group for the scalar path.

steps.title: Compare complete work boundaries

quiz.prompt: What makes two instruction-work measurements comparable?

choices.text: The same input and function boundary.

steps.expectedObservation: The complete decoder includes validation costs that a direct kernel measurement omits.

hints.text: Choose equal observation boundaries before comparing costs.
Count from each whole-function entry through its return, including validation, frame handling, guards and called kernels; record the same raw input pattern.

steps.prose: Measure the complete scalar and vector entries after both accept the same data. Include validation, frame handling and tail work. Keep kernel-only observations separate, and record the binary pattern and text length used for each result.

steps.title: Verify canonical round trips

quiz.prompt: What should a completed free-writing check require?

steps.expectedObservation: Equivalent complete implementations agree on results and state obligations.

hints.text: A round trip alone can conceal matching encoder and decoder mistakes.
Compare each direction with an independent host codec and canonical re-encoding, then add malformed padding, capacity and exact in-place cases.

steps.prose: Use the independent host encoder and canonical decoder check, along with byte ownership and error cases. Repeat calls in one execution session using actual prior output. Guided states describe this construction; completed free-writing checks can accept another correct allocation or algorithm.
